name: Threonine
info: A hydroxyl group and two chiral centers. It can be phosphorylated.

history.clue: The name is connected with the sugar threose and the spatial arrangement of its groups.
history.story: In the 1930s, William Rose's group discovered that rats did not grow on a mixture of all the amino acids known at the time. The search for the missing component led to threonine: the compound was isolated in 1935, and its spatial structure was clarified in 1936. It was named for the similarity of its group arrangement to that of the sugar threose.
